what_happened: A docs job to re-study how firstmate handles work and rebuild the explainer page was rejected at final verification. The verifier found that the reading of the request was wrong, so the passing acceptance criteria did not show the request was met (major finding). It also found a second major problem: the quotes and line numbers were read from the mounted source tree but labelled with commit 6407052f, while Athena had pinned the source for this job to fc8972cd. A reader checking the page at the labelled commit could find lines that do not match. No individual acceptance criterion or check is listed as unmet.
cause: Two gaps allowed this. First, the reading was accepted without the user confirming it against the request, so criteria derived from it could all pass while the request went unmet. Second, the commit label and the source actually read come from two separate places (the pin file and the mounted tree) with no code check that they are the same. The label was written independently of what was read, and the mismatch was found only by the verifier at the end, which wasted the whole job.
prevention: Add a code check that runs before the verifier. It reads the commit of the mounted source tree and compares it with the pinned commit in pin.json. It also compares both with the commit label in every claims and rationales file, and it fails the job early on any difference. Also have the reading restate the request's end outcome in one sentence and check it against the request before work starts, so a misread is caught at admission rather than at the final verdict.
proposed_request: Re-study how firstmate handles work and rebuild the explainer page so a newcomer can follow it, with every quote and line number cited from one pinned source commit. Before the verifier runs, add a check that the mounted source tree, the commit in pin.json and the commit label on every citation in claims.json and rationales.json are all the same commit, and fail the job early if they differ. Outcome: the page's citations match the pinned commit, so an outside reader who checks them at that commit finds the quoted lines. Restate your reading of this request in one sentence for confirmation before you start.
